```{r}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(MatchIt)
library(survey)
library(cobalt)
library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv("data.csv")  

summary(data[, c("y", "selfrpt", "mindset", "test", "sch_race", "pov", "size")])

#EDA

# Histogram of achievement scores
ggplot(data, aes(x = y)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "orange", bins = 30, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Achievement Scores", x = "Achievement (y)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# Density plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = mindset, fill = factor(z))) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("magenta", "orange")) +
  labs(title = "Mindset Score Distribution by Treatment Group",
       x = "Mindset Score", fill = "Treatment") +
  theme_minimal()

# Scatter Plot of Mindset vs Achievement
ggplot(data, aes(x = mindset, y = y, color = factor(z))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("magenta", "orange")) +  
  labs(title = "Mindset vs Achievement by Treatment",
       x = "Mindset Score", y = "Achievement", color = "Treatment") +
  theme_minimal()

# Heatmap 
numeric_data <- data %>% select_if(is.numeric)
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data)
cor_df <- melt(cor_matrix)

ggplot(cor_df, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Correlation Heatmap ",
       x = "", y = "") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1,
                                   size = 10, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
# 1. Linear Regression

# Basic model
lm_model <- lm(y ~ z + selfrpt + gender + race + fgen + urban + mindset + test + sch_race + pov + size, data = data)
summary(lm_model)

# ATE and 95% CI
lm_ate <- coef(lm_model)["z"]
lm_ci <- confint(lm_model)["z", ]
cat("Linear Regression ATE:", lm_ate, "CI:", lm_ci, "\n")

ate_df <- data.frame(
  term = "Treatment (z)",
  estimate = lm_ate,
  lower = lm_ci[1],
  upper = lm_ci[2]
)

# Plot
ggplot(ate_df, aes(x = term, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "purple") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.1, color = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Estimated ATE from LR",
       x = "", y = "Effect on Achievement") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# For linear regression the estimated ATE is 0.4126, meaning that on average students who received the treatment scored 0.41 points more than those who did not, after accounting for all observed covariates.

# The confidence interval is [0.387, 0.437] meaning we are 95% confident that the average effect lies between in this interval.

# Since p-value is less than 2e-16, it is highly statistically significant, meaning the treatment has a positive effect on student achievement.
```

```{r}
# 2. IPTW

# propensity scores
prop_model <- glm(z ~ selfrpt + gender + race + fgen + urban + mindset + test + sch_race + pov + size,
                data = data, family = binomial)
data$prop_score <- predict(prop_model, type = "response")

# Compute IPTW weights
data$weights <- ifelse(data$z == 1, 1 / data$prop_score, 1 / (1 - data$prop_score))

# Diagnostic plot
love.plot(
  bal.tab(prop_model, weights = data$weights, method = "weighting", estimand = "ATE"),
  colors = c("purple", "orange"),
  thresholds = c(m = 0.1),
  stars = "raw",
  abs = TRUE,
  var.order = "unadjusted"
)

# Propensity Score Distribution 
ggplot(data, aes(x = prop_score, fill = factor(z))) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Propensity Score Distribution by Treatment Group",
       x = "Propensity Score", fill = "Treatment (z)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Weighted regression
des <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~weights, data = data)
iptw <- svyglm(y ~ z, design = des)
summary(iptw)

# ATE and CI
iptw_ate <- coef(iptw)["z"]
iptw_ci <- confint(iptw)["z", ]
cat("IPTW ATE:", iptw_ate, "CI:", iptw_ci, "\n")
```

```{r}
# After applying IPTW, the estimated ATE is 0.4145 with a 95% CI of [0.382, 0.446].

# The covariate balance plot shows strong improvement after weighting.
```

```{r}
# 3. Doubly Robust Estimation

# regression model
dr_model <- lm(y ~ z + selfrpt + gender + race + fgen + urban + mindset + test + sch_race + pov + size, data = data)

# Predict estimates with and without treatment
data$mu1 <- predict(dr_model, newdata = data %>% mutate(z = 1))
data$mu0 <- predict(dr_model, newdata = data %>% mutate(z = 0))

# DR estimator
dr_estimate <- mean(
  data$z * (data$y - data$mu1) / data$prop_score +
  (1 - data$z) * (data$y - data$mu0) / (1 - data$prop_score) +
  data$mu1 - data$mu0
)

cat("Doubly Robust ATE:", dr_estimate, "\n")
```

```{r}
# Doubly Robust combines outcome regression and IPTW weighting and estimated ATE as 0.4144.

# The result is similar to linear regression and IPTW estimates, which reinforces the positive effect of treatment.
```

```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Number of bootstrap samples
num_boot <- 100
dr_ates <- numeric(num_boot)

for (i in 1:num_boot) {
  # Resample with replacement
  boot_data <- data[sample(1:nrow(data), replace = TRUE), ]

  # Fit bootstrap model
  boot_model <- lm(y ~ z + selfrpt + gender + race + fgen + urban + mindset + test + sch_race + pov + size, data = boot_data)

  m1 <- predict(boot_model, newdata = boot_data %>% mutate(z = 1))
  m0 <- predict(boot_model, newdata = boot_data %>% mutate(z = 0))
  eps <- 1e-6
  ps <- pmin(pmax(boot_data$prop_score, eps), 1 - eps)

  # DR estimate for bootstrap sample
  dr_ates[i] <- mean(
    boot_data$z * (boot_data$y - m1) / ps +
    (1 - boot_data$z) * (boot_data$y - m0) / (1 - ps) +
    m1 - m0
  )
}

# 95% CI 
ci_dr <- quantile(dr_ates, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
cat("Bootstrap 95% CI for DR ATE:", ci_dr, "\n")

# Histogram of bootstrapped ATEs
dr_df <- data.frame(dr_ate = dr_ates)

ggplot(dr_df, aes(x = dr_ate)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "purple", color = "black", bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(dr_ates), linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Bootstrapped ATEs from DR",
       x = "DR ATE", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Based on the doubly robust method, the growth mindset intervention led to an average increase of ~0.41 points in student achievement.
# With 95% confidence, the true effect lies between 0.383 and 0.441.
```
